title: Petition to Rename Nashville International Airport to Dolly Parton International Airport Gains Momentum
text:
A grassroots campaign to rename Nashville International Airport after Dolly Parton has garnered significant support, with lawmakers pledging to introduce legislation and discuss further honors for the late icon. Parton's legacy continues through her theme park and upcoming projects.
A petition to rename Nashville International Airport to Dolly Parton International Airport has gained significant traction, with over 117,000 supporters. The initiative, started by a group of fans, has received a boost with Tennessee State Senator Jeff Yarbro pledging to introduce legislation to make the change happen.
The group expressed gratitude for his support, stating that Dolly Parton deserves to be remembered and celebrated in this way. Parton herself made a rare public appearance in June at the opening of Dolly's Tennessean Travel Stop in Cornersville, Tennessee. Tennessee state Rep. John Mark Windle has also shown support for the petition, acknowledging Parton's impact on the city.
Meanwhile, lawmakers are discussing ways to honor Parton's legacy when their legislative session begins in January 2027. Dolly Parton's team has announced that the Dollywood theme park will remain open, carrying forward her message of love, perseverance, and hope. They also revealed that Parton was working on several projects before her death, including Dolly's Tennessean Travel Stops and Dolly Parton's SongTeller Hotel.
The future of these projects and Dollywood remains uncertain, but the team has assured fans that they will keep Parton's legacy alive
